reason: The passage presents King Josiah as a model of exemplary leadership, explicitly characterized by humility. When confronted with the Book of the Law—which implicitly critiques previous practices—Josiah responds with humble submission. The prophetess Huldah specifically commends him: 'Because your heart was tender (רך־לבבך) and you humbled yourself (וַתִּכָּנַע) before the Lord when you heard the words of the Law.' His leadership model includes tearing his garments, seeking divine counsel, and implementing sweeping reforms based on what he learns. The text establishes that good kingship involves receptiveness to correction and humble obedience before God's word, even when it requires acknowledging previous shortcomings and making difficult changes.
